findings.title: Where kids' events are most often free
findings.text: Across all 42 metros, 33.6% of the 7,041 dated events in the next 30 days are free. The highest free shares are in [Denver](https://grassyknees.com/denver) (69% of 369), [Raleigh](https://grassyknees.com/raleigh) (66% of 77) and [Cleveland](https://grassyknees.com/cleveland) (64% of 58); the lowest are in [Providence](https://grassyknees.com/providence) (17% of 52), [Pittsburgh](https://grassyknees.com/pittsburgh) (18% of 179) and [Philadelphia](https://grassyknees.com/philadelphia) (20% of 202). (Metros with at least 50 upcoming events.)

findings.title: What a paid kids' event costs
findings.text: The typical metro's median paid ticket is $19.25 (median of 42 metro medians; usually one child's ticket as the organizer lists it). The most expensive are [San Francisco](https://grassyknees.com/san-francisco) ($29.95), [Houston](https://grassyknees.com/houston) ($29) and [San Antonio](https://grassyknees.com/san-antonio) ($29); the cheapest are [Washington](https://grassyknees.com/washington-dc) ($10), [Raleigh](https://grassyknees.com/raleigh) ($11.50) and [Cincinnati](https://grassyknees.com/cincinnati) ($12).

findings.title: What kind of activities there are
findings.text: Community is the largest category: 32.9% of 14,988 current listings, ahead of Arts & crafts (24.8%) and Outdoors (13.7%). It leads (or ties) in 38 of 42 metros; the exceptions are [New York](https://grassyknees.com/new-york) (Arts & crafts), [Boston](https://grassyknees.com/boston) (Arts & crafts), [San Francisco](https://grassyknees.com/san-francisco) (Arts & crafts) and [Minneapolis](https://grassyknees.com/minneapolis) (Arts & crafts).

findings.title: Free-heavy metros are not necessarily cheaper
findings.text: Across the 41 metros with at least 50 upcoming events, there is no rank correlation between a metro's free-event share and its median paid ticket (Spearman's rho = -0.04). A metro with many free events does not reliably have cheaper paid ones.

findings.title: Read the counts as catalog coverage, not per-capita supply
findings.text: Current listings per 100,000 residents range from [Denver](https://grassyknees.com/denver) (25.2) down to [New York](https://grassyknees.com/new-york) (2.9), with a median of 10.2. Large metros are not proportionally larger in the catalog, so compare shares and medians across metros, not raw counts.
